title: Why Your Cat Walks On You At Night (The Survival Instinct)

blocks.text: You wake up at three in the morning with your cat marching heavily across your chest.

blocks.text: First, those delicate paw pads are actually highly sensitive temperature sensors.

visual.subject: cat's paw pad
visual.action: hovering just above the blanket, sensing invisible heat radiating

blocks.text: A cat's base body temperature is around thirty-eight point five degrees Celsius.

visual.subject: sleek black cat
visual.action: sitting upright, displaying a calm but alert resting posture
visual.framing: medium shot of the cat isolated on the bed
visual.details: ilustração felina editorial, sleek black cat with yellow eyes and a red collar, dark blue blanket, no text

blocks.text: This is significantly higher than yours, meaning they burn heat rapidly at night.

visual.subject: sleek black cat
visual.action: shivering slightly or pulling its paws inward looking for warmth
visual.framing: close-up of the cat tucking its paws
visual.details: ilustração felina editorial, sleek black cat with yellow eyes, dark blue blanket, no text

blocks.text: Stepping in various spots is their tactical way of scanning your body.

visual.details: ilustração felina editorial, sleek black cat paw, dark blue blanket, no text
